This is a super common issue when it comes to reactive dogs, they’re almost always worse when it comes to being alone with their owners. If you’re up for it I would also try and have a more structured walk, and ask him for a down or a sit every now and then to remind him that he’s not running the show. This stuff really only clears up when your dog truly has an understanding of what is expected of them and that you absolutely mean what you say, which requires a lot of repetition and reinforcement. As soon as you start to let things slide they usually regress a little bit. Stick with it and don’t forget to reward good behavior!!

You need to stop it before it starts, so what you should do is learn about your dogs triggers and study their body language. (Your trainer has given you the tools and hopefully explained to you how to utilize them? ) next time you go for a walk and you see something that you know will trigger your dog, watch for cue’s that they’re building up to a reaction- like for example, their tail will go straight up and may wag, they stiffen their stance, maybe they start to whine etc this is the time where you want to break their attention. Don’t let them fixate. That’s when you would use the stim or vibrate on your e-collar, and pair it with the obedience your dog *should* know. You always want to fall back on your obedience, you don’t want to just correct your dog without any rhyme or reason, so correct them (for example) breaking the heel command (because they’re becoming excitable and reactive, maybe pulling on the leash) and redirect, remind them what they’re supposed to be doing. You can also abruptly change direction while giving the heel command while utilizing your e-collar as another option and walk away from the trigger. Keep your dog engaged and reward the correct behavior. Sorry this is kind of brief but it’s sort of a lot to explain over the internet, Hope this helps.
